deploy.check: With a four-queue config on the live store, `kbu council jobs status` reports four live queue children with per-queue claimed/in-flight/pending counts, and resuming job 96a612a03a2149c5935478d519f9f522 settles items on at least two seats concurrently (argo progressing while a codex call is in flight) -- the condition that was impossible under the shared FIFO.

REQUIRED_OPERATOR_STEP_BEFORE_RESUME.what: `kbu council db migrate` must be run against the live store BEFORE the four-queue resume, and it must run while the council is STOPPED.
REQUIRED_OPERATOR_STEP_BEFORE_RESUME.why_it_is_required: The seat-filtered claim index ix_calls_status_seat_not_before is backfilled onto an existing store by SqliteStore.add_missing_indexes(), which is reached ONLY from SqliteStore.migrate(). migrate() has exactly one call site in the codebase -- CouncilUtils.db_migrate() (council_utils.py:315-354), i.e. the `kbu council db migrate` command. It is NOT called from init_schema() and NOT called on store open. So the live store does NOT acquire the index by being opened; without this step the partition fix lands and the resume still scans and sorts ~57,000 pending rows on every claim, and the index is the last place anyone would look for the cause.
REQUIRED_OPERATOR_STEP_BEFORE_RESUME.why_it_must_run_STOPPED: db_migrate() acquires the execution lock with kind `migrate`, which is EXCLUSIVE on the store-wide lock. Queue workers and the controller hold that lock SHARED. So the migrate cannot run while the council is up -- it will be refused with LockHeld naming the live holders. The ordering is: stop the council -> kbu council db migrate -> start the four-queue council -> resume job 96a612a03a2149c5935478d519f9f522 by job_id.
REQUIRED_OPERATOR_STEP_BEFORE_RESUME.cost_and_safety: Measured ~49 ms to build the index on a synthetic 57,000-row calls table (2 ms for a no-op rerun) against SQLite's 30 s busy_timeout, so the migrate window is negligible. db_migrate() takes a backup of the store file first. The backfill is idempotent (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, honoured by the installed SQLAlchemy 2.0.52 SQLite dialect) and only ever CREATEs -- it never drops, rebuilds or reorders an index.
REQUIRED_OPERATOR_STEP_BEFORE_RESUME.verified_not_to_break_supersession: The backfill is general over declared indexes, so it also recreates the PARTIAL unique index ux_calls_one_live (unique over five columns WHERE live). Proven empirically against a real database: the backfilled definition reads out of sqlite_master as `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_calls_one_live ON calls (job_id, item_id, role, seat_name, upstream_digest) WHERE live`; two colliding superseded (live=0) rows are ACCEPTED and a second colliding live row is REJECTED with IntegrityError. Had the predicate been dropped, a roster change superseding pending calls would have raised on exactly this store.
REQUIRED_OPERATOR_STEP_BEFORE_RESUME.observability_gap_noted: db_migrate()'s report names the COLUMNS added (it calls add_missing_columns() itself, before migrate(), specifically so it can report them) but does NOT name indexes added, because add_missing_indexes() runs inside migrate(). So the report may understate what it did. Cosmetic; worth a follow-up if operators rely on that report.
